findings.evidence: Lines 175, 230, and 254 use only `hB x`, `hA x`, and `hA y`, respectively; lines 262–274 use membership only for the two factors. Line 294 invokes the pointwise closed-ball lemma. The existing `tateGauge_lt_iff` at line 112 already uses the weaker element-specific signature.
findings.fix: Require power-membership only for the compared element in the first three lemmas, for both factors in `tateGauge_mul_le`, and for `x` in `tateGauge_eq_zero_iff_forall`; pass the global hypothesis at seminorm construction sites.
findings.issue: Global localization assumptions unnecessarily restrict `tateGauge_le_zpow_mul_tateGauge`, `tateGauge_le_zpow_iff`, `tateGauge_mul_le_of_mem`, `tateGauge_mul_le`, and `tateGauge_eq_zero_iff_forall`. These statements also apply to eligible individual elements in an ambient ring that is not globally localized.

summary: Several pointwise gauge lemmas unnecessarily require every element of the ambient ring to admit a power moving it into the subring, preventing their use for individual eligible elements.
